issue_context.title: [Transform] Continous transform failure when grouping dates using terms agg
issue_context.body:
Originally reported on discuss: [discuss](https://discuss.elastic.co/t/next-checkpoint-progress-total-docs-remains-empty-after-first-checkpoint/251729/7)

**Affected versions**: 7.5 - 7.11

When dates are grouped as `terms` (exotic use case, normally dates are grouped using `date_histogram`), the field value that gets created in the transform destination index is a number:

expected: `"2020-10-16T07:27:44Z"`

actual: `1602833264028`

The same problem applies to continuous transform when it searches for changes after checkpoint 1. The transform fails after injecting the wrong format into the query, see full trace below.
 
**Mitigation**:

Check if you can use another non-date field for `terms`. If that's not possible, reindex the source data and create a keyword field from the original date field and `group_by` the newly created field. The pipeline created for re-index can be used for newly incoming data as well as for historic data.

ok, the code comment is outdated, will change it. What this does is basically rewriting the config to the latest format. The problem is as follows, a transform `<7.11` will write millis, `7.11`> will write strings (note the version is the version of the transform, not the es version). If update is called, it always updates the version field, a former `7.6` transform becomes a `7.11` transform. But that would mean that this transform starts writing strings. That's why we inject the `dates_as_epoch_millis` into the config, so it still becomes a `7.11` transform config, but with `dates_as_epoch_millis:true`.
